one who erred and did not pray minchah on Shabbat prays two weekday [Amidot] at the close of Shabbat
he recites havdala in the first [of the two], and does not recite it in the second
and if he recited havdala in the second and not in the first, the second counts for him
...the first does not count for him
is that to say that since he did not recite havdala in the first, he is as one who did not pray, and we make him go back?

because he can say it over the cup
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: the prayers -- the Patriarchs instituted them
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: the prayers -- they instituted them corresponding to the tamid offerings
Abraham instituted the morning prayer
as it is said: 'and Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood' (Gen 19:27)
and 'standing' means nothing but prayer
as it is said: 'and Pinchas stood and prayed' (Ps 106:30)
Isaac instituted the afternoon prayer
as it is said: 'and Isaac went out to converse (lasuach) in the field toward evening' (Gen 24:63)
and 'conversation' (sicha) means nothing but prayer
as it is said: 'a prayer of the afflicted when he is faint, and pours out his sicha before the Lord' (Ps 102:1)
Jacob instituted the evening prayer
as it is said: 'and he encountered (vayifga) the place and lodged there' (Gen 28:11)
and 'encountering' (pgia) means nothing but prayer
as it is said: 'and you, do not pray for this people, nor raise cry or prayer for them, and do not entreat (tifga) Me' (Jer 7:16)
[the Sages said:] the morning prayer until midday
for the morning tamid may be offered until midday
R' Yehuda: [the morning prayer] until four hours
R' Yehuda: for the morning tamid may be offered until four hours
[the Sages said:] the afternoon prayer until the evening
for the afternoon tamid may be offered until the evening
R' Yehuda: [the afternoon prayer] until plag hamincha
R' Yehuda: for the afternoon tamid may be offered until plag hamincha
[the Sages said:] the evening prayer has no fixed [time]
for limbs and fats not consumed from the evening are offered throughout the night
[the Sages said:] the additional prayer all day
for the additional offering may be offered all day
R' Yehuda: [the additional prayer] until seven hours
R' Yehuda: for the additional offering may be offered until seven hours
which is minchah gedolah? from six and a half hours onward
which is minchah ketanah? from nine and a half hours onward
R' Yehuda's plag hamincha is the plag of the LAST minchah (the resolution of the iba'ya: first or last?)
R' Yehuda: they said the plag of the last minchah, and that is eleven hours less a quarter
the Patriarchs instituted the prayers, and the Rabbis attached them to the offerings
for if you do not say so -- according to R' Yosei b'R' Chanina, who instituted the additional prayer?
